key_insight: Counterfactual bias in open-source LLMs for pediatric ED triage varies widely by model and does not reliably improve with larger size or medical-domain pretraining.
clinical_relevance: For clinical decision support, even small demographic or context changes can shift triage predictions, so fairness audits are important before deployment.
method: Compared 10 open-source LLMs, including base, instruction-tuned, medical-domain, and fine-tuned Qwen/MedGemma/MedLLaMA/GPT-OSS variants.
Used paired clinical vignettes with only one counterfactual change at a time across demographic, socioeconomic, access, behavioral, social, and system-context factors.
Measured any shift, undertriage, overtriage, >1-level shifts, mean shift, and mean absolute shift in pediatric ESI prediction.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, the fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B had the lowest sensitivity (5.27% any-shift; mean absolute shift 0.0534) versus 16.02% and 0.1706 for the base model, with other models sometimes performing worse.
watch_item: Counterfactual audits reveal sensitivity patterns but do not by themselves prove real-world clinical safety, and results may depend on the vignette set and prompting setup.
paper_title: Counterfactual Auditing of Bias in Open-Source Large Language Models for Clinical Triage
